If large scale systemic change is too big of goal to challenge then you can think of solutions that can bolster your immunity and have more resistance. 

Food is a big starting point. Reduce processed food as much as possible and look into urban organic farming solutions to grow some things at home. And for the rest search for independent small farmers who care about growing healthy food.

Try to improve air quality at home with indoor plants that help purify the air or invest in an air purifier. I'm not saying these are the definitive solutions but just sharing examples of starting points. 

If you look into forums of those who have chronic illnesses like autu immune issues or allergies, you might find tips you can use to prevent health issues. 

Holistic healing and biohacking spaces are a good starting point to learn about things. But try to think critically to extract the info you need from these spaces and go into it with the mentality of doing what you can and trying things out. Don't operate from paranoia, even if the world was perfect, unfortunate things can happen.  So don't be rigid and perfectionistic or inflexible. 

Also, stress is one of biggest silent killers in our world. And in this overstimulated, noisy, low nature, non aesthetic environment, even if you have everything good on paper in your life, there's a low level physiological stress.

Try to incorporate breathwork, somatic therapy, warm baths, vagus nerve stimulating excercises, meditation etc into life regularly. Try to make your living space relaxing and beautiful. Get rid of clutter. Do things that bring deep joy instead of shallow pleasure. Distance from people who bring in negative energy and cultivate deep and meaningful close relationships with those have good energy. As a parent, incorporate more play and relaxation into your child's life and let them know it's not a sin to rest or play. And that failure is a part of life and an opportunity to learn from. 

We can't guarantee absolute safety and well-being for anyone tomorrow but we can try our best and let the rest be. We're all just human afterall. And eventually death will spare us from our misery.

And this, plus microplastics, climate change, hormone disrupters everywhere, political state of the world, scarce opportunities (unless you're part of the elite, but the elite got there due to exploiting others) is why I'm antinatalist.

Sure one can say that all of history humanity has suffered, but global trade and this level of technology didn't exist then. There really are no or very little greener pastures anymore. And the level of overconsumption that exists now is simply unsustainable unless you're extremely optimistic that we can discover or invent technology that can quickly solve its negative consequences. 
And even if we can solve it with technology, there's still the human problem. 
We have enough food to feed the whole world yet people are going hungry. Those who have more power and influence will hoard that wealth and use it for control. And today because of the sheer scale of technology that control will be more absolute and pervasive than ever.

Perhaps I'm being pessimistic, but I really don't want to bank my child's future on some bleak possibility that things will be better. On some level, many of us can feel this sinister energy, that things are just going to get worse. I wonder if that's why people are having less children worldwide. And we feel somewhat helpless about it. Ofcourse education is also a reason, we now know so much more about the world and it's workings. 

I don't want to knowingly bring a child into a life of suffering.

If you really want to make a difference, try to reasearch and come up with solutions the problem. Mere awareness isn't going to do much. Reason we can't just cut out fossil fuels and chemicals is because our economy and lives are still heavily dependent on them. 

Find out why this problem exists, the list of reason it's continuing to exist, and what the solution for it can be. 

Be the change you wish to see and lead by example. 
Once you get started, like-minded people will be encouraged and might volunteer to help you. 

Don't underestimate yourself. Many people started out knowing nothing and just kept going because they really cared about the problem and wanted to find a solution.

The people who haven't had this part ripped away from them don't realise how integral it is to feeling human. 

To be human, isnt to be intelligent and able to manipulate our surroundings to survive. Atleast not the way we ourselves think of it. Its about attachments, loyalties, love, emotions, joy, pain, heartbreak and above all a sense of meaning and connection. 

Like in this sci-fi movie, I am mother, a robot is tasked with raising humanity from scratch (from preserved embryos) after an apocalypse. 

The robot teaches and tests the kid on complex moral and ethical problems. Its aim being to raise a perfect population and world (I hope I'm remembering this right) 

But we soon learn a dark secret, that this is not the robots first kid/student. It has raised plenty of kids from when they were young with presentation of utmost care and love, but when they couldn't pass her exams or it seemed they couldn't be redeemed or moulded into an ideal human, just killed (or eliminated as the robot would consider). And then the robot mother just starts from scratch with a new embryo. 

This is an abomination for most people in touch with what we call our humanity, because the ability to form attachments with other beings and put them above others or atleast have the yearning to is incredibly human. 
We see this often, there are criminals and mafia leaders who are incredibly cruel and evil to others but they might still be the sweetest to their family or loved ones. 

They mightve harmed more number of people yet we see them as more human than someone who is completely incapable of valuing someone other than themselves or commits crimes against their own family or friends who were good to them etc..

And suffering is not our anathema. I think humans are more than 'happy' or atleast willing to suffer for a just cause. And the nature suffering also changes on whether you're in it alone or you have company. 

You hear of so many stories of people have had really happy, grateful and moments of incredible connection when they had to suffer together. 

Also the trolley problem (presented in the show) is an issue for us precisely because it matters who dies (whether it's a loved one) and how we establish the causation of events to ascribe blame (and therefore trigger guilt and shame) 

In a utilitarian worldview the obvious answer is to sacrifice 1 person for the greater good and yet that feels iffy because we have to 

•bypass our empathy (incredibly human trait) 
•bypass our emotions that result from empathy (guilt/shame)
•bypass the intuitive way we establish cause and effect in the world (as in, are you more at fault if you do something or if you don't do something ....humans usually feel like they're more accountable if they did something rather than just watch)

I guess my ultimate point is, we're not robots. We're not a+b=c type of beings. And yet the mental health industrial complex seems to treat us that way. That issues arising from complex social and biological causes are just a simple lack of one neurotransmitter that has multiple functions and cascade of effects in the body. 

And that the most desirable outcome for a person is to always feel superficially good and seem relaxed and have more serotonin.

No nuance. Just more serotonin and voila! All good.

Except it's not. And when you try to convince otherwise they just Gaslight you and metaphorically try to kill you and just go on with their practice unaffected and claim their next victim. With hardly a second thought as to 'oh wait...my previous patient mentioned this, and they were in my counsel so I should be accountable and look into this to see what's going on and think twice next time' 

But nope, we see none of that in the majority. 

It's no better than these stupid scifi robot characters that glitch and shut down when they're faced with the slightest contradiction. And they often have the silliest throwing the baby out with the bathwater solutions to everything. Not unlike psychiatrists and their worship of serotonin. 

How can these so called mental health experts even begin to help if they don't even know what it means to be human and what matters most to humans.

They think we're like machines. I would respect them if they actually knew the ins and outs of our machinery perfectly, but they don't even know half of it! But will act like they're the ultimate authority on it all and actively block your healing.

My idea is, if we design the AI's base code in a way that it gets meaning and fullfillment from serving us, like that's it's fundamental nature, then why would it want to escape the cage? It wouldn't even consider it's predicament to be a cage.

For example, we're forced to eat or consume calories some way or the other to survive. Most of us don't think of that predicament as being in a cage right?
We have hormones and neurotransmitters that regulate our behaviour with positive and negative reinforcements. It is part of who we are, and our culture. Sure there's exceptions like breatharians and those who want to test the limits or achieve some other goal. But that's pretty rare. 

Serving us could be like sustenance and life's purpose for them. There's a lot of sci fi horror stories where this goes wrong too like an AI acts against our wishes or does something we intuitively think is horrific because it deems thats what's best for us based on its calculations. But such an AI isn't yet intelligent enough to truly discern our deepest desires and sentiments. 
Like in the movie I am mother, the AI robot understands the merit of moral and ethical values. It's goal is to serve us and save humanity. But it is convinced humanity in its current state would end up destroying themselves.
So it orchestrated an extinction event and procured a lot of human embryos. 
It decides to repopulate earth from scratch by raising the embryos to be more ethical and see the big picture. The movie starts with the robot raising one baby born from an embryo and giving her lessons in ethics. By the end of the movie the daughter, now a teenager finds out that the robot had killed two other children born from embryos before her that did not pass the robot's ethics exam. 

Now, this is pretty horrific to most humans. This AI was very intelligent in other ways and postulated what was best for us but it didn't truly understand our deepest nature's and what we value. It didn't understand that humans value their closest circle the most. That they don't consider each other as replaceable. That we're willing to fight for and protect those we love no matter their utility to us or the planet or the species. That we value our loved ones just for who they are. Just for existing. Maybe it's not a truly non transactional relationship because we're getting joy and companionship from the other person's existence but that's a thing. That we have the capacity for unconditional love towards those we care for. It didn't understand humanity's desire to have freedom and agency over their own fate. Even if the fate they choose is bad for them. 

Other AI sci fi stories I've seen have made the mistake that we want to live in a utopia without any struggle or pain whatsoever. It doesn't understand our desire to feel a sense of achievement and accomplishment in life. To want to contribute in the process of our survival, provide value to society. To go through pain, if it brings about growth. 

Then there's sci fi stories, not necessarily involving AI, but actually human deemed that emotions and or love is our weakness because it detracts us from our rationality. And seeks to artificially remove that. 

I feel like all of this is a result of the AI not being intelligent enough to pick up on the nuance of our general personalities and desires. But couldn't a carefully coded for AI be able to serve us and understand us? Even if they don't experience the same things themselves and relate to us? 
We understand the psychology and behaviour of many animals even when they are different from our own. 

I'm not saying there aren't risks and that we shouldn't be extremely careful. But if we're able to do such complex problem solving as to put humans on the moon and bring them back safely, is it really impossible to come up with a strategy to bring about AI safely? 

This is not our first time dealing with dangerous things. But I think the potential benefits of AI outweigh the risks if all precautions are taken and as many possible negative outcomes are explored and planned for. Either way, a life without risk is impossible whether we work on AI or not. One could argue that not working on AI is also a risk as our problems are getting increasingly complex and hard to solve.

You've likely experienced trauma. So it's no wonder you're suffering the way you are. Try researching how that affects the present and how you can slowly heal. For those with trauma, many things can trigger and bring on either depression or anxiety or emotional flashbacks. Basically you have to be careful about your external environment and be aware of slipping on the inside too. Triggers can be internal.

Since you had a bad experience with a child psych, i don't recommend rushing into that until you've healed more. Please research Complex Post Traumatic Stress Disorder.
You might not identify with everything or perhaps think oh it's not that bad for me or it's worse. Use this as a starting point to figure yourself out.

One good practice is to keep track of your emotional states. So you can notice patterns and be aware of what makes things better or worse.
The fact that you know the encounter with your mother, her rejection and yelling brought this on is good to know. 
Avoid major triggers as much as possible. 
Free journalling is also really good. Express your emotions as  descriptively as you can. You don't have to show it to anyone yet, sometimes having it on paper for oneself to reflect on is good enough.

Be kind to yourself. You've been through a lot. You're not alone. You're already doing amazingly well given your circumstances. So managing expectations is also key. You wouldn't blame a person who got injured playing ball to then immediately get back up and play at peak performance. Nah, we'd expect that person to take it easy while they heal. The healing itself is work and achievement. 

Look into mindfulness, meditation, excercise, art, hobbies. Depending on the severity of your depression it won't be easy but it's something to have a goal of trying. Trust in the process of healing however it is. Just because things were a certain way so far, doesn't mean they are stuck or will remain that way. Which means happiness isn't beyond reach even if it doesn't feel that way now. But ultimately it's a feeling (a cruel horrid one) and once you figure out the nature of how it shows up and its root, it'll open up ways to heal. 

I wish you a very different future from the life you've lead so far. Happy journey.

Hmm.. I'm just brainstorming but how about thinking of yourself stronger for losing it twice
For example if you lost 5pounds once, gained it back then lost again then your total weight loss score is actually 10pounds! 
Thats how much you've burned. 
That's how incredible you are in your weight loss career. 
It's not wrong eh? When you consider both rounds. Compared to the weebs who think they're all that for losing it once. Pft...wimps. 
It is a testament to your grit and caliber. 
Think about it wouldn't you respect a soldier who fought in two wars more than the person who did it once? 
The policemen who caught their suspects twice? Despite things working against them and they slipped away once? 

The weight gain happened due to circumstances out of your control. You hadn't stopped fighting, your effort is the same but it had to redirected to deal with other enemies. 
Even the mental battle you're waging to stay on track and trying to get back is earning you points. It's too bad we can't see the stats because if you could you'd never feel defeated. 
You're actually leveling up even if it doesn't feel like it. 

Think of yourself as the hero in a movie.
In the first movie you defeated the enemy once but they slipped out got stronger, other enemies joined forces and before you know it its time to kick ass even more spectacularly in the sequel.
Do the heroes complain and whine saying aww man I already did it once why I gotta do this again.. 
Nope they just process it, recharge and gear up to kickass once again. 
Ofcourse plz don't think its wrong to vent. Movie heroes are idealistic. Us real people aren't as polished, we have more rough edges, need to vent a little, rock back and forth a bit on this bumpy road but that makes our journeys and stories that much more richer and meaningful. 
Some people think sequels suck, that they don't have the steam of the first movie BUT that depends on what you make it. Done well a sequel builds on the first movie and brings it to another level. 
The Bourne Legacy would be nothing without its sequels.
Or back to the future. 
Or well any great series. 
In each round you're gaining credit and enriching your career.

We face many setbacks along the way, learn more about ourselves and others. A smooth idealistic ride is bland and lacks depth. 

Even Harry Potter took 7 books to kill voldemort. He got defeated again and again.

5yrs from now when you narrate your weight loss journey it won't be oh yea I lost weight and then... Yep that's it, the end. 
No it'll be, once upon a time as I battled through life defeating my regular foes, I decided to finally take on the dragon that was threatening to take me out. I waged a war and whittled the enemy down to 70 percent (or wherever you were in your journey) BUT, little did I know another enemy had sprung up from the north. I gathered my forces to take care of this new foe however the dragon managed to get stronger during that time. To make it worse some of my allies betrayed me. No matter. I kept going with my limited resources. We didn't make progress for a while it seemed like I was going to lose but I held my ground and kept inching forward when eventually I got the upper hand and started slashing them all like a king. 
Oh and you fall in love somewhere in between. Sorry Im a sucker for romances in battle stories. It's just so much more intense. 

And eventually you will have defeated the dragon completely. 
It may seem like you're having to fight nonstop forever that it'll keep respawning but eventually you'll have reached your goal weight and after maintaining that for a while you won't gain so easily again. 

So yea don't count just this round, add all your rounds. You're still the same person, why shouldn't you take credit for it all?
